CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules (workflow, r-package, ci, native-code, correctness, assurance) come from the r-skills plugin’s rules/, loaded at session start because of the marker above. Never copy them here. Where this file and a shared rule disagree, this file wins for this package. Cloud sessions do not load the plugin and run without them.

What this is

zutable gives R typed tables: a data.frame that always knows the name, logical type (Arrow’s) and nullability of every column, queried through a bracket whose named arguments are SQL’s clauses (where, select, by, having, order, limit, distinct) over bare column names. The bracket is captured and translated into typed expressions over a closed vocabulary, so every result’s schema and every type error is known before data is touched; the same plan runs in the package’s own executor, over a file scan, or as SQL in DuckDB or zuspark. := updates existing columns in place through C. Beneath the local executor sits a grouped kernel (group, sort, join, reduce) with a C header for siblings. No Imports; LinkingTo: zufast from the first kernel code; every reader and engine is in Suggests. It deliberately does not invent an engine, add columns to an existing table, copy data.table’s surface beyond the bracket and :=, use threads, or exceed 2³¹ − 1 rows.

The specification is .agents/design.md (from RFC 0074) with the kernel in .agents/design-kernel.md (from RFC 0037). They outrank this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides. Decisions marked (C) there are the RFC’s and may be overturned by the maintainer; (M) are the maintainer’s.

Current state

Scaffolded 2026-11-16 with create-pkg.sh (C via use_c()). Stages 0 to 8 (2026-11-17) built the table, the bracket, := and joins over the reference executor; Stages 9 to 15 (2026-11-17 to 19) the kernel beneath it, its header, consumer fixture and fuzz target; Stage 16 (2026-11-19) the benchmark record in .agents/benchmarks.md, the README, the evaluated Get started vignette and two articles under vignettes/articles/; Stage 17 (2026-11-19) the assurance pass over native coverage, fuzz reach and mutation survivors. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0; for now 0.1.0 includes the kernel (design D35).

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1 for v0.1.0. Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: none. Planned header consumers (zucsv, zuxlsx, zudedup, zulm) are listed in design-kernel §3. zutable cannot reach CRAN before zufast (on CRAN since 2026-11-16) and needs zuarrow’s release for its Arrow paths.

Commands

The shared commands, and for the kernel:

sh tools/ci/c-tests.sh                        # C tests without R, ports included
R CMD INSTALL --preclean . && Rscript tools/run-benchmarks 1e7

Benchmark only after --preclean: load_all() leaves -O0 objects in src/ that a plain R CMD INSTALL reuses.

Architecture

To be written as stages land; see .agents/design.md. The scaffold set up C through use_c(): src/zutable.c registers the routines and src/numbers.c wraps zufast’s number parsing and formatting (LinkingTo: zufast). src/altrep.c is the sorted-values ALTREP class (D22, D46): its payload is copied before any write when shared, and every write drops its marks. src/join.c is grp_join()’s translation of zutable/join.h; join() runs on it, with the R join kept as its oracle under options(zutable.executor = "reference"). src/reduce.c is grp_reduce()’s translation of zutable/reduce.h; the executor’s aggregates, over() and := with by rewrite each aggregate call into a column of per-group values (zt_eval_groups() in R/execute.R), keeping the loop over groups as their oracle, and the loop for an r() node. The kernel’s header goes under inst/include/ and src/ stays a thin R translation over it (design-kernel §4).

Invariants that are easy to break

These are fixed by the design before any code exists:

  • No Imports. Every sibling and engine is Suggests; a type whose vector lives in an absent sibling is a zutable_type_error naming it, never a silent degrade to double or character.
  • No route changes a table’s schema. :=, $<-, [[<-, [<- keep the column set and types; names<- and assigning NULL are errors.
  • zt_commit() swaps column pointers and never writes into a vector, so a vector shared with another object is never corrupted and copy() duplicates only the list. It also enforces freeze() and clears column properties.
  • Every operator has a reference implementation in R over base, written first and kept as the oracle for the kernel (D29). Do not delete it when the C version lands.
  • The plan keeps the six lineage rules of design §8.5 from the first commit (resolved references, kept expressions, source identity, …), although lineage is not exported in 0.1.0.
  • The kernel header compiles as C11 without R under ZT_STANDALONE, and as C++17 (design-kernel §4, §8); nothing in src/ is an algorithm.
  • Errors are base-R conditions under zutable_error; no cli or rlang.

Testing

Conformance suite: none yet; DuckDB is planned as the oracle for the emitters and vocabulary (design §14). Helpers: none yet. Runtime: none yet.

Continuous integration

Calls the shared r-actions workflows r-cmd-check.yml (profile auto, plus in the full profile a Windows R-devel row, nosuggests and nold; weekly on Mondays 02:41 UTC), native-checks.yaml (sanitizers with ASan, valgrind, lto, rchk, analyzers, cran-special; valgrind reads tools/valgrind.supp, which suppresses only findings whose top frame is in DuckDB, the test oracle), gctorture.yaml (step 2000 on pull requests, step 20 daily and on dispatch), alloc-failure.yaml (weekly, through tools/alloc-exercise.R, which must reach every native routine), coverage.yml (badge on gh-pages; native: true, so it lists the C functions no test enters and the conditions taken one way), mutation.yaml (Mull over the six C test binaries, built with ZT_TEST_QUICK by tools/ci/mutation-build.sh, and the fuzz driver; a survivor is real only when no binary kills it) and assurance.yml (ungated-jobs: fail), plus r-lib’s pkgdown workflow. Dispatch gctorture at step 20 on the branch (gh workflow run gctorture.yaml --ref <branch>) before merging a change to PROTECTs. Step 20 sets ZUTABLE_GCTORTURE=true, under which the pure-R typing sweep, the many-size sort sweeps, the kernel join differential and the million-row tests do less (tests/testthat/helper-0-torture.R): the whole suite outgrew the 240-minute job by Stage 11, and again by Stage 13. platforms.yaml runs tools/ci/platform.sh on each OS: check-headers, the C tests with the fuzz target’s 20,000-input smoke, and the consumer fixture (tools/ci/consumer.sh, which builds tools/zutabletest against the installed header and runs it with zutable gone from the library). fuzz.yaml runs the kernel’s fuzz target (tools/fuzz/, without R) for 30 seconds on a pull request and an hour weekly and on dispatch, with reach-floor: 97. Stages marked full in the roadmap: 3, 6, 10, 11, 12, 18, 19, 20.

Tests run shuffled everywhere: tests/testthat.R and tools/ci-run-tests.R print their seed, and ZUTABLE_TEST_SEED replays an order.

Vendored native code

Nothing is vendored as a file. Three sorts are ported to C from their C++ originals, each in its own template under inst/include/zutable/ with the original’s notice and a list of what was altered, and in inst/COPYRIGHTS and Authors@R: pdqsort (zlib, orlp/pdqsort at b1ef26a) in pdqsort.inc, Vergesort (MIT, Morwenn/vergesort at a1a5081) in vergesort.inc, ska sort (Boost 1.0, skarupke/ska_sort at 2c14d4b) in skasort.inc. tools/ci/fetch-originals.sh fetches the originals at those commits, checking SHA-256, for tests/c/ports; a port changes only with that test. fluxsort, crumsort and swenson/sort are not vendored (D41).
